commands.command: read spikes.jena_marking.adapter (OCOR-DEV-0018) in full and confirmed no pyshacl (or any general SHACL processor) is a project dependency (checked ocor-runtime/pyproject.toml and uv.lock) -- decided the smallest contract-compliant SHACL-equivalent for this task's own scope is an explicit, closed required-property/closed-predicate shape check expressed directly in Python, rather than adding a new external dependency (a new pyshacl dependency would require pyproject.toml/uv.lock changes outside this task's own expected_file_areas and outside the smallest-slice principle)

design: publish(resource_id, properties) validates the closed predicate vocabulary (ALLOWED_PREDICATES) and the required-property set (REQUIRED_PROPERTIES) and a non-empty, well-formed provenanceRef BEFORE issuing any SPARQL write -- an unauthorized predicate or lossy/missing provenance blocks publication entirely (the task's own two negative acceptance criteria, made structural); list_authorized/exists_authorized reuse the exact real marking-join pattern OCOR-DEV-0018 already proved (a resource is never returned without its classification joined in the same query); to_json_ld is denied via exists_authorized for any clearance that does not authorize the resource, then serializes via a real SPARQL CONSTRUCT + rdflib Graph.serialize(format='json-ld') -- a real JSON-LD serializer, never hand-rolled

applied the OCOR-DEV-0037 lesson proactively: the fault-injection test expects the real raw urllib.error.URLError (a genuine connection-refused failure), not a translated JenaAdapterError, since _request only translates HTTP-level error responses -- no bug needed fixing this time because the lesson was applied up front

requirement_results.command: a publication satisfying the closed shape and non-lossy provenance is readable and serializes to real, well-formed JSON-LD via rdflib
a predicate outside the closed vocabulary blocks publication entirely (UNAUTHORIZED_PREDICATE) -- no triple is ever written, verified by an empty authorized list afterward
a missing required property blocks publication entirely (SHAPE_VIOLATION), verified by an empty authorized list afterward
an empty or fabricated provenanceRef blocks publication entirely (PROVENANCE_INVALID) -- the task's own second negative acceptance criterion, made executable
list_authorized returns only resources at or below the requester's real clearance, reusing OCOR-DEV-0018's marking-join pattern
the authorized count never diverges from the authorized list length; the raw, marking-blind count would leak but the public API never exposes it
to_json_ld is denied (MARKING_DENIED) for a clearance that does not authorize the resource, identical to the marking-safe read path
a real Fuseki unreachability (a genuine closed local TCP port) propagates as a real urllib.error.URLError before any triple is written, never a partial publication
full local pytest regression with a real live PostgreSQL DSN set, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline (the two known interpreter-pin failures are unrelated and pre-existing)

residual_risks: This adapter's SHACL-equivalent is an explicit, closed required-property/closed-predicate check rather than a general SHACL processor (no pyshacl dependency exists in this project); a future task adopting a richer, arbitrary SHACL shape vocabulary would need to add that dependency deliberately, which is a policy/dependency decision outside this task's own smallest-slice scope.

publish's atomicity is a single SPARQL INSERT DATA statement covering exactly one resource's triples; a caller publishing many resources from one C3 commit would need one publish call per resource, matching the closed-shape validation's own per-resource scope.

The pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope; it produces the same 2 pre-existing, unrelated regression failures documented in every prior evidence file this session.
rollback_procedure_verified: Every test resets the real Fuseki dataset via adapter.reset() before running; verified directly by 4 consecutive full test-suite runs with no manual cleanup between them, and by every blocked-publication test proving the authorized list stays empty afterward -- no partial triple ever survives a rejected publish.
